CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain after skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
42-year-old female presents with right index finger pain sustained during a skiing accident approximately 5 days ago (last Saturday). Patient was skiing double black diamond slopes when she lost control, flipped down the slope, and jammed her index finger on an object during the fall. She is the only injury sustained from the accident. Pain is rated 7 out of 10. Patient has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not applied ice or worn a splint prior to this visit. Physical examination reveals tenderness to palpation and manipulation of the right index finger. X-ray of the right hand shows no fractures; all bones and joints are in normal alignment. Clinical examination and imaging findings are consistent with a sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation. Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in skiing activities, including advanced slopes.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger: tenderness to direct palpation, pain with passive extension and flexion, pain with compression over the DIP joint and proximal interphalangeal joint. Right hand x-ray: normal, no fractures, all joints and bones in proper alignment.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: normal, no fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal joint of the right index finger. Plan includes: (1) splinting of the right index finger; (2) mobic 15 mg orally once daily for 14 days as anti-inflammatory; (3) follow-up visit in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
